summary.title: How Does a Database Work? (Writing a sqlite clone from scratch in C)
summary.one_liner: A multi-part tutorial walking through building a simplified SQLite-style database in C, from a REPL and SQL compiler to persistence and B-tree indexes.
takeaways: How a database stores rows in memory and on disk, and when data moves from memory to disk
How to build a REPL, a simple SQL compiler, and a virtual machine that executes statements
How a B-tree is laid out as leaf and internal nodes, including binary search and node splitting
How cursors give a uniform way to scan and modify table data
summary.summary: This is a 15-part tutorial in which the author builds a clone of SQLite from scratch in C to learn how databases work. It moves step by step from setting up a REPL and a minimal SQL compiler and virtual machine, to an in-memory append-only single-table store, then persistence to disk and a cursor abstraction. The later parts cover B-tree design: leaf node format, binary search with duplicate keys, splitting leaves and internal nodes, and scanning a multi-level tree. The page itself is an index of these parts and does not contain the code, and the project is noted as no longer under active development.
